text:
alex: heads-up — we got a burst of 413s from a customer sending mixed-dimension vectors in one request. console preflight didn't catch the dimensionality mismatch and the error message is unhelpful.
priya: ugh. do we have an example request from logs?
alex: snippet from nginx logs:
```
POST /v1/embeddings
Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"input": [[0.1,0.2,... 1536 floats], [0.3,0.4,... 768 floats]]}
Response: 413 Payload Too Large
X-Request-Id: r-abc123
```
priya: 413 feels misleading if it's really a dims validation problem. clients assume they can batch mixed dims. we used to return 400 with explicit message.
jordan: can we add a quick preflight check in the router that returns 400 + human message when mixed dims are detected? also include an HTTP header with expected vector length.
sam: +1 on preflight. but watch perf — we already do cheap validation in the gateway. adding per-request content scan might increase CPU on hot routes.
lin: what if we expose a `X-Embed-Dim` hint header or a `preflight=true` endpoint? console could call it before sending big payloads.
priya: `X-Embed-Dim` header sounds ok for well-behaved SDKs, but still need server-side detection for legacy clients.
alex: telemetry question — we need to distinguish real 413s (bytes) vs our new dims-413. add metric `embed.reject.dim_mismatch` with tag `mode=preflight|runtime` so we can tell how often console/SDK preflight prevented it.
jordan: also emit `embed.request.max_dim` and `embed.request.total_bytes` so we can tune default max payloads and show guidance in console.
sam: for rollout UX: we should soft-deprecate allowing mixed dims. proposal: 1) add preflight 400 + human message; 2) console warns and auto-splits only for a period; 3) after N weeks, reject mixed dims by default. plan needs telemetry to see how many clients rely on it.
priya: agree. console auto-split is a huge UX win but we need to be explicit about cost (doubling requests increases token cost). show a modal: "split request into 2 calls — estimated cost + latency".
lin: implementation detail: splitting at the console level means we need to add an internal route to batch and re-order responses. can we reuse existing `embed-splitter` lambda?
alex: yes, reuse but add a `preserve-order` flag in case payload included per-item ids. also add `X-Embed-Trace: splitter-v1` header for tracing.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot updated: staging router patch (preflight check) deployed at 1965123500 — rollout=1/3.
jordan: nice. priya, can you add the telemetry keys to the ingest contract? I want dashboards: "Dim mismatch rate" and "Auto-split success rate".
priya: on it. also adding a console preflight call with a 2s timeout and clear error mapping: 400 -> "dim mismatch"; 413 -> "payload too large"; 422 -> "mixed dims auto-split failed".
sam: last thought: quota semantics — if we auto-split, we should charge both requests against the same original quota token but mark them as "split-part" in billing events, so customers aren't surprised by apparent duplicate charges in console metrics.
alex: good point. add `billing.meta.split_origin_id` so we can collapse in billing UIs.
lin: I'll prototype header wiring + trace IDs today.
alex: thanks. if anyone sees customer hits on prod we should abort split and fallback to returning explicit 400 until switch is safe. tagging @priya for dashboards & @jordan for router observability.
priya: pinged dashboards ticket, adding panels and alerts.
jordan: watching staging metrics now. ping when canary finishes.
deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary rollout to prod scheduled at 1965123600 if no regressions.
